entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abu Sulayman Banakati (born unknown, died 1330) was a renowned historian and poet of the late Ilkhanate era.

He is best known for his Persian world history book, the Rawdat uli al-albab fi maʿrifat al-tawarikh wa al-ansab, also referred to as Tarikh-i Banakati.

Banakati's work offers valuable insights into the Ilkhanate's significant cultural and intellectual achievements, including the patronage of scholars and artists.

His contributions to the field of Persian historiography have had a lasting impact on the study of Islamic history and culture.

One of the most fascinating aspects of Banakati's work is its detailed account of the Mongol Empire's expansion and the subsequent establishment of the Ilkhanate.

As a historian and poet, Banakati's work not only provides a unique window into the Ilkhanate era but also highlights the importance of cultural exchange and the transmission of knowledge across borders.

Banakati's Rawdat uli al-albab is a testament to the enduring power of Persian literature and the impact of the Ilkhanate on the development of Islamic civilization.
